utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. A good question. It wasn't only a question of food and medical assistance. We had also other problems, mistreatment, beatings, harassment. In view of the fact that in the camp, access was given to people like Lugar, I could personally observe such scenes, and this was also one of the topics. And all the complaints went -- they had to go to Mr. Krunic, and then he formulated the sentence which the interpreter conveyed to the International Red Cross and the other gentlemen. Therefore, all of us had to address Mr. Krunic, and it was he then who formulated the sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, I'd like to take you back now to your reaction to hearing this conversation between Mr. Krunic and the ICRC delegates. You addressed them in English, telling them of your problems. What did they do in reaction to this information?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the fact that I directly addressed, I requested that a medical doctor be brought in, and if they could assure -- ensure a minimum of food supplies. Mr. Krunic turned red and he said that the special police would immediately take me to the doctor, the physician in Bosanski Samac. It was really a precedence that somebody would leave this camp. The international authorities were surprised, and pleasantly surprised by this gesture. They, in fact, offered a vehicle which he turned down. He said that he had special police forces which would accompany me, escort me, so that nothing would happen to me on the way.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did the delegates of the Red Cross ask you any follow-up questions directly about the conditions in the camp?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But this meeting soon ended. Krunic said that the topics had been exhausted, and I was happy to receive that promise that a medical physician would be visiting us in Zasavica in the next day and that we would be receiving minimum food supplies. And that surprised me. And so the meeting ended rather soon, rather quickly.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: What kind of follow-up questions did the ICRC put to you?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely concerning the issue of the doctor, the issue of survival, how the food situation -- and the topic of mistreatment and beatings.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were you able to tell them frankly what the situation was, including whether people were mistreated or beaten?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Concerning the beating and mistreating, at that point in time I didn't dare say anything, because I was afraid I wouldn't survive until the next morning. Krunic knew that Lugar had already been in my home, and no need to tell you what kind of a murder [As interpreted] that was. And Krunic knew what was happening in that village. And I was afraid of not surviving the next morning; therefore, I had to keep quiet about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you convey to them the situation of lack of food and lack of medical care?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My complaint was in mild terms. I only asked for a visit of a doctor, and if they could help and bring in some food supplies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. It's page 44, line 18. I believe that this witness said that it was not a kind of murder that was, but the right sentence should be what kind of murderer he was. That was the B/C/S version of the words of this witness, and the transcript should be clarified and corrected. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, I believe this is just a typing error on the transcript, but did you describe Mr. Lugar as a murderer?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so, and with reason. If you wish an explanation, I will furnish it.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: No. That's not necessary. But perhaps you could just say -- you had information that he had killed people, that's why you call him a murderer; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And he was allowed to come to Zasavica and wander around the camp in Zasavica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. You testified about a promise made to take you to the doctor. Were you taken from Zasavica to visit a medical doctor?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They allowed me to change my clothing, put me in a vehicle, and - the special unit from the 4th Detachment - took me to Dr. Nogic, a gynaecologist, a Muslim, of Muslim ethnicity, and worked in the health centre in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: After Mr. Nogic had conducted an examination, did he recommend to the authorities what treatment you should have?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Dr. Nogic was shocked by my general condition. He turned to their representative, who was standing there by, and at the same moment I should be taken to Belgrade and that it's a very, very complicated disease, illness.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: When he said you should be taken to Belgrade, did you understand that to mean where there were proper medical facilities?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was precisely the reason. I would have to undergo an operation, and that could be only performed in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: The people he told this to, were these armed people who had accompanied you from Zasavica to the health centre?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, members of the 4th Detachment under arms, who even wanted to be present at the gynaecological examination. He stopped-- Dr. Nogic stopped them in front of the screen which was around the examination table, but they were there.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: What was the response when Dr. Nogic said that you should be transferred to Belgrade for proper medical treatment?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They said that that was out of the question, completely out of the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: What other course of action did Mr. Nogic recommend for your condition?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said -- namely, he requested that if I cannot be transferred to Belgrade, that then they should bring me in on a daily basis for injections.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Is that what happened, then? Were you brought to the health centre on a daily basis for injections?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I am grateful that they kept their promise, and they did take me every day for injections, and they saved my life, which later on became more complicated.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: For roughly how many days after this first visit did you continue to get these daily injections?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was allowed to have a course of injections of ten days. That was the course.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Apart from the time you were taken to have these injections, did you have to remain in Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Immediately after the injection, I was taken back to Zasavica.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Would you be taken under guard each time there and from Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, armed guard, even when I was receiving the injection.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: What happened to the other people in Zasavica? Did they get a visit by a medical doctor?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the next day, Dr. Ruzmir came and examined all of those who had complaints, and in the same way, the next day, some food arrived. I remember that I received a litre of cooking oil.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did other types of food arrived? You said you received some oil. What other types of food were distributed to the people in the camp?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Some flour, depending on the number of family members, and some noodles. Some received some rice.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Until this food distribution, had there ever been food distributed by the authorities to you detainees in Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Nothing of food arrived to Zasavica. It was only from Zasavica that the remaining food was taken out by the military who would enter Zasavica.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Whilst you were there, did military personnel come to take food from Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. They would take food out.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did individual members of the military come to houses looking for food, or was this done in an organised fashion?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two ways of doing it: In an organised fashion, as I lived in that house, which was a pig farm, they would take, in an organised manner, pork meat and pigs to the families of the killed soldiers. That was done by the military. Individually, they would come into our homes and take the few potatoes and peppers which we found in these homes where we lived. So they had the right of taking that away. So both of it occurred: Organised and non-organised.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Was there an exchange of people from Zasavica organised in the few day after the ICRC visit?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. An exchange was being planned, and indeed I was very happy at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were you advised that you would be part of this exchange?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was informed about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And can you tell us: Was this one or two days after the ICRC had visited?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was the second day after their visit.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And was it after you had had your diagnosis by Dr. Nogic?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, after that.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: How did you learn that you were to be included on this exchange?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Svetozar Vasovic came to me and said that I should get ready because I am on the list for the exchange which is expected to take place rather soon.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were you advised that you were on the list because of your medical condition?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not concretely because of that, but that I should get ready and that I will be on that list.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: This Svetozar Vasovic, did he work for Miroslav Tadic?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was his assistant.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you see him in the building where you went when you went to speak with Miroslav Tadic?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in order to arrive to the office of Mr. Miroslav Tadic, I had to pass through the office of Mr. -- by the office of Svetozar Vasovic, for all information he would inquire with Mr. Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Was the first time you saw Mr. Vasovic in Zasavica when he came to tell you that your name was going to be on the list, or had you seen him prior to this?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This wasn't the first meeting of ours in Zasavica. I saw him there on numerous occasions.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And each time he would come, would it be in connection with exchanges?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, it wasn't in connection with the exchanges.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Why did he come to Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the reasons was to collect food for himself.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Was this food from houses or food from the pig farm you described?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exclusively from the homes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were you -- you were told that you were going to be on the exchange. Were you actually brought to an exchange point? Did you actually get exchanged a few days later?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was told that I'd be exchanged, indeed they did come and pick me up in the early morning and took me to the football pitch in front of the secondary school, and the other people on the exchange list were already there, so that I came to the right place.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were you the only one taken away that morning from Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't the only one. Some ten, approximately ten people from Zasavica, between seven and ten, were involved.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were these women, children, elderly persons? Who were the other persons brought with you for exchange?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Detainees from Zasavica, primarily elderly women and children.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. You said you were brought to the football pitch. The other people on the exchange were already there. Who were the other people on the exchange list that you saw gathered at the football pitch?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Along the school itself, people were lined up, people who came from the prison in Samac. So it was the school, the staff headquarters, and the police station. So these were people from these detention facilities. They were pitiful and beaten up. On the next area, there was the family members who came to accompany these people, and in the third group, consisting of myself and the other persons who came from Zasavica.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And these people who had been brought from detention centres, were they exclusively non-Serb?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Men, non-Serbs, who were brought out from these camps. I knew most of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: How were these people who were gathered there, including yourselves, organised into buses for the exchange? What exactly took place?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In front of these detainees, the military and the police were standing, and they were reading out names and surnames: That and that person, after the name had been read, would have to head for the bus, and prior to entering, boarding the bus, his name would be read out again, and only then he can board the bus. So first these men, these detainees from these prisons, were the first ones.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Was your name called out?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was. Finally, also my turn came, my Pegi. The two of us headed towards the bus, because my name and surname was clearly read out from that first list. When I came to the bus, before the door, bus door, Naser, known as Cakara, stood. He looked at me and he said that my name is not on his list.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: What did you do when he told you that your name did not appear on the list?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First I was shocked, and I said that possibly there was a mistake, that he should check properly that list. Well, he was very rude, and he didn't have the time to discuss it with me, that not to move and not to leave. Then I just moved from the bus door. The police then came and took me away from that field.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And where did they take you?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the first moment, I thought that I'd be free at last to go home, if I can't go into the exchange, but they took me to the third camp, and that was the secondary school.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were you put into the gym hall in the secondary -- in the main building of the secondary school or were you held in a corridor?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First they kept me in the hall. Then they told me to go into the classroom. Then they didn't know what to do with me, and I didn't know what to do with myself either.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you spend the day, then, in the secondary school?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I sat there in the secondary school until the evening, when the police came and took me back to Zasavica, to the same house from which I had been taken away happily that morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: After you returned to the house in Zasavica, how much longer did you have to stay in Zasavica for until you were actually exchanged?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stayed until the 5th of November, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: During -- after your return to Zasavica and up until the 5th of November, 1992, did you have to perform -- continue to perform forced labour?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. My treatment was continued during that period of time. I went to get shots. The doctor made a certificate which stated that I should be relieved of all physical work, and to my great surprise, this is exactly what happened. I was spared.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you then stay in the house that you had sheltered in Zasavica or were you required to work in the confines of Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In the answer of Mrs. Kapetanovic, the last answer, page 52, line 20 and -- between line 20 and 23, we clearly heard in B/C/S version that Mrs. Kapetanovic said that according to the certificate of the physician, she was relieved of all work and work obligation, these particular words we heard. And I kindly ask that this part of the transcript should be corrected in that sense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That is what is contained. She was relieved of all physical work.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, she said, in fact, work obligation, not only physical work. She said physical work and work obligation, which might be of the importance for our case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, if you can recall, what was it that the physician certificate relieved you of? Do you remember what terms were used?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document, the paper that I received from Dr. Nogic, clearly stated that he asked that I be relieved of all physical labour and work obligation. It's stated precisely what I told you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Notwithstanding the certificate from the doctor, were you required to carry out some work within the confines of Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the day that my treatment was finished, this is to say on the day when I was given my last shot, I had to go and work in the makeshift kitchen in Zasavica. So I wasn't said to work in Odzak, but I rather remained in the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And in this makeshift kitchen in Zasavica, what sort of work would you be carrying out in the kitchen?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We -- or rather, I had to do work, at the disposal of the men from Krajina. I had to cook, prepare coffee, tea, even bake a cake, whatever they demanded.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And these men from Krajina, were they based in Zasavica or did they have a stopover point that they would call into? What were they doing in Zasavica that you would tend to them in this manner?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The men from Krajina were stationed in Obudovac. Since Zasavica was transformed into a pigsty, which is what we called it, because it was simply flooded with stolen pigs. Our people had to slaughter the pigs, not only for the purposes -- for the use of the 4th Detachment members, but also for the men from Krajina. And they would come, and while they were waiting for the pigs to be readied for them, they were in the house of Mrs. Blanka.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And so you worked in Mrs. Blanka's house in the makeshift kitchen; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you continue to do this up until the 5th of November, when you were exchanged?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: How did you learn that you were again put on an exchange list in November?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After several attempts to get my name put on the exchange list, women from Zasavica, Marta and Blanka, attempted to help me. At that time I only assumed that my name would be put on the list.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Who were these attempts made to?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Svetozar Vasovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And what sort of attempts were made to put your name on the list? How did Marta and Blanka help you with these attempts?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They told me that without money or something that I could offer in exchange, I had no chance of getting myself on that list.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did they tell you why they knew you needed to be able to offer some financial consideration for your exchange?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because women and families that had already been exchanged had given money for their freedom. I knew those families personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Can you recall now who any of those families were that provided money to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember the family called Cosic. I remember a girl named Senada or Senija. I remember other people, but cannot tell you their names right away. But I know for a fact that the Cosic family had given money. People were paying somewhere around 500 German marks to gain freedom.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And to whom was this money being paid?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Svetozar Vasovic. He was in charge of us, and he was the only one who came to see us regarding the exchange.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And this is the man who had his office as the assistant to Miroslav Tadic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did Marta and Blanka help you to offer money or valuables for your exchange?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Since I used to help them while we were imprisoned in Crkvina, they wanted to repay me by paying for my freedom.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Just on that, these two women, Marta and Blanka, they were from Zasavica, were they?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, both of them were from Zasavica.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: They were Croats?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Catholics.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I understand they were also detained back in May with you in Zasavica -- in Crkvina. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, both of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So what did they use to pay for your freedom?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Blanka did not have anything she could offer, but her sister-in-law, Marta, showed me a cistern of oil, a set of curtains, and tried -- and said that she would try to use that and 100 or 200 German marks to buy my freedom.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: This oil, is it cooking oil, or it's gas for a machine or for cooking oil? What sort of oil was it?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Marta's house had central heating, so this was fuel, oil, for central heating, what is normally used for that purposes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Did Marta in fact offer this cistern of oil, the curtains, and this spare money she had to get your name on the list?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After showing all this to me, she said that she would give all that to buy my freedom, and she said that to buy her own freedom, she would take something from the house of her brother-in-law, whatever was left after plundering, in order to gain her own freedom.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you witness her making the offer of these goods to Svetozar Vasovic in exchange for being put on the list?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Naturally. Otherwise I would not have been put on the list. All of that would be taken, but my name would not be put on the list.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: You were physically present yourself when this offer was made to Vasovic?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And did you hear him accept the offer?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said that the deal was good.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Was your name put on the list?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My name was finally put on the list, or rather, it was put on the list again.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were the names of Blanka and Marta also put on the list?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just Marta's name.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Who told you that your name was on the list and that you should get ready for being exchanged?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the eve of the exchange, Vasovic came and read out the names of all of those who were to be exchanged the following day. So it was Vasovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And on the following day, were you instructed to all gather at a particular location in order to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were told to come at 7.00 in the morning to a place near the spot where the road turns to Zasavica, and they would come to get us.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And when you went to that place in the morning, were you loaded onto buses?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Sometime around 9.00 they came, and we finally started boarding the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: The buses that came, the vehicles, were they empty or did they already have other people to be exchanged on them?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were already almost full.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And they were full with what kind of people? Women, children, detainees from other locations? Who was on these buses?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were detainees, the remaining detainees from the school, from the TO; there were non-Serb citizens who had not been arrested but their names were on the list; there was a truck full of dead bodies; and there were us from Zasavica.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Approximately how many from Zasavica were you that day?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you the exact number, but there were many of us.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: When you boarded the vehicles, where were you taken to? What was your final destination point?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were taken to a place in Croatia called Dragalici, near Lipovac, in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: When you arrived at Dragalici, did you see the defendant Miroslav Tadic there?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him there.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you personally have any conversation or discussion with him, or did you just see him present?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I simply saw him, but I didn't want to come to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: What did you have with you when you arrived at Dragalici? What had you been able to rescue from your former life in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was wearing my shabby clothes, torn-up clothes. I had my Pegi with me, with a bag with an album, and some clothes of my husband, and that was all.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: The clothes you were wearing, were they clothes that you had originally been arrested in bag in September?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And the album, this was a photograph album of memories from Bosanski Samac; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had the fortune of having Luka Culumovic take the bag, in which there was a photo album. I have to tell you that this is the only thing left to me after 35 years, and these photographs are the only thing that document my life before the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: In fact, you had with you just the bag which Luka Culumovic had given you when you were arrested in September, and I think you told the Bench you had Pegi with you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My Pegi was with me the entire time, and she was exchanged in Dragalici as well. So I had this bag and Pegi.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Were you allowed or permitted to go back to your apartment in Bosanski Samac to collect some other personal items to take with you?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not for a moment such alternative was presented.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you -- Mrs. Kapetanovic, would you say that on that day in Dragalici that you had chosen of your free will to leave Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is something I could never claim. Even nowadays, when they asked me where I'm from, I say that I'm from Bosanski Samac, although that is not true, not true any more. I would have never left Bosanski Samac on my own free will.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: When you were exchanged in Dragalici, did you then cross into Croatia?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was simply transported through Croatia and taken to Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: You were transported through Croatia, and where finally were you brought to?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the end, I crossed the river in a raft, and I was taken to Domaljevac, where we were helped by the HVO army. From there, I was taken to Grebnice, and I came to the front line.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you receive some medical attention for the condition you were diagnosed with when you were detained in Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Bosnia, I did not receive any kind of medical treatment, but in view of the fact that my family was from Croatia, I managed to establish contact with a doctor. I went to Zagreb, and there I finally realised how weird life was. The doctor told me that my diagnosis was cancer and I was given some three to five years to live.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you finally, with your husband, obtain refugee status in a European country? I think I can say Germany, since you told us that you speak German now.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The following year, since I had Croatian papers, I had no difficulties in going to the West. So I came to Germany, and the following day upon my arrival, I had surgery in Germany. My husband also came to Germany after fleeing the front line.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: After you moved to Germany, did you make attempts to reclaim your property in Bosanski Samac municipality?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I attempted to do that. However, it was very difficult to achieve it when living in Germany.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you finally manage to get back your flat?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I finally managed to recover my flat, but only the flat.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And when did you finally gain back possession of your flat?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received the decision concerning the flat two years ago, but I didn't manage to complete the process two years ago. I simply received the decision concerning it.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: This decision entitled you or stated that you were the owner of the apartment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you then take steps to sell that apartment?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The sale of the apartments in Bosnia became legal, and I was able to buy back my apartment and then sell it.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: You said that that was your -- you only got back the apartment. Do I understand that you still have legal claim over a house in Bosanski municipality that is the subject of a property dispute? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly so. My late husband and I built a house in a village 12 kilometres from Samac. The village is called Donja Slatina. And to this day, I was unable to solve this issue with my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your flat, when you did get it back, what was the condition of the flat? Were the possessions you had left behind still there, and was the house capable of living in?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I came, entered the first time this apartment again with my husband, it was the first and the last time, it was with a heavy heart, enter an apartment which was -- the door was opened by another person. And in that apartment, I didn't find a single object, item, belonging to me. Everything had been plundered. The lady in question had repainted the apartment and brought in her own belongings. It was clear to me that this wasn't a place for me any more.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. It's 12.30. I understand that's the time for the break, is it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We will resume at 12.50 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy. You're continuing.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, the lady who had moved into your flat and brought her possessions, was she of Serb ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, she is of Serb ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And did you -- she is the same person you sold your flat to after you regained possession of it; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did she demand some money from you?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. She asked for money for the renovation of the apartment.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And did you have to pay her?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She asked of me three and a half thousand German marks, because she had repainted the apartment, had the apartment disinfected, made a chimney. The apartment is located in the central part of a big building. There was a lot of work, but although I wasn't interested in that. The apartment, when I left it, was in order, was in excellent shape. I wasn't interested in this. She didn't have to do all this work, and this figure was absolutely too high.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you have to pay her the three and a half thousand Deutschmarks?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the negotiations and agreement on the price per square metre, at the end I had to pay those three and a half thousand Deutschmarks.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you receive any compensation for the loss of your personal property or the use of your apartment after you had been expelled from Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Something happened which was like a punishment to me. I purchased that apartment, which I had to pay for a price. It was -- but I already paid for it, but I had no documentation of that. Plus, I had to pay the three and a half thousand Deutschmarks for the renovation of the apartment.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: You had paid for the flat before the conflict, had you?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was -- we bought it the moment when we moved in and when the building was completed. I don't recall the exact year.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Did you ever see that man Svetozar Vasovic, who you had paid to put you on the exchange list, again after you had been exchanged?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see Defence counsel on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object to this question because the Prosecutor [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... Svetozar Vasovic who you had paid? [Interpretation] The question concerning the question of Svetozar Vasovic, it was -- he said that the deal was acceptable. So here it's leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the witness has testified that there was oil, curtains, and a number of hundred Deutschmarks given to Mr. Vasovic to put her on the exchange list and she was present when that took place. I can clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. What the Trial Chamber understood, was that when the witness said that he had said that was acceptable, that means that he accepted those goods and the money.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We didn't hear whether the witness paid or that he took anything, accepted anything. But here in the question that -- it's been already accepted. But during the direct examination, we didn't hear that the witness has paid or that he has accepted. But now in the question, it's been said that it's been paid. It is this question that I object to.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I'll ask again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I don't understand the point of your objection. Anyway, Ms. Reidy, you can clear that with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I think you've understood the nature of the discussion going on, Mrs. Kapetanovic. Did you pay Mr. Svetozar Vasovic to have your name put on the exchange list?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question of Mr. Vasovic is correct, and I stand behind that which was happening then. So I was present at the deal which was acceptable. But as this question has been raised, let me say this act took place. I've been informed. I said that Blanka and Marta took the initiative for my freedom. Marta went with me and Blanka stayed behind. So the woman I contacted later on told me that this had been done. The offer has been -- was acceptable and the offer was then also implemented.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, you had said earlier on the record that you were physically present when this offer was made to Mr. Vasovic and that he said that was fine, the deal was done. Is that correct, that you were there when all this was -- when that exchange was going on?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The discussion took place in front of me and the deal was acceptable. That was the sentence expressed in front of me. The exchange took place after I left, but the deal went through, and I was informed that this was paid.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And so who told you that the goods were handed over and the money was paid?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had the opportunity of talking to Blanka when I was set free, and also when Blanka was free.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And Blanka confirmed for you that the offer of the oil, the money, and the curtains had in fact -- or the consideration of those items had in fact been given and accepted by Mr. Vasovic?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Immediately after we left Zasavica.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, this Mr. Vasovic, you said that you saw him again after you had been exchanged. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him in my lawyer's office.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Was this in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And did you -- did he address you in any way or did he talk about the exchange?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. We did not talk about the exchange. That belongs to our past. He only asked about my health; that was all.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, in the period between you giving your testimony here a few weeks ago and now, has any approach ever been made to one of your relatives about your testimony?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was during the time that I was here the first time.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And who made an approach to your relatives?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The wife of Miroslav Tadic met at the market my mother-in-law, came up to her and said -- she said, "Mirsada, do you know where your daughter-in-law is?" And my mother-in-law, a very fragile woman, was a bit scared. She said, "Yes, I do know." She turned and went back home without doing her shopping. And she didn't go out of the house again.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Is your mother-in-law living in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My mother-in-law is living with her husband, who is handicapped and is in a wheelchair.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions of this witness at the moment. I do, however, have the outstanding matter of three maps which currently have a status of -- three diagrams produced by this witness, and they have currently an ID status, so I'd just like to move that they get fully entered into evidence. Those are Prosecution Exhibits P68, P69, and P70.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I just wanted confirmation from the registry assistant that they're all -- they were marked for identification only. That's P68, P69 and P70.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours. P68 ID, P69 ID, P70 ID, they are all diagrams and they remain as documents at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I want to find out from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honours, I'm not objecting of admission of these schemes. There is only one thing. We would like just to clarify with our colleagues from the Prosecution if these schemes were actually made by the witness or according to witness's testimony, someone from the Prosecution made actually those schemes. This is the only thing that I would like to find out. We don't object to that, and we should --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. What is the position, Ms. Reidy?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: They were drawn up on a computer, in fact by me, according to the witness's instructions. There had been a hand diagram drawn. I duplicated that on a computer for clarity's sake and asked the witness whether or not that was an accurate recording of what she told me to draft. So they were done according to instruction by -- but not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: By the witness. Yes. All right. Can we have them -- can we have confirmation that they retain the same numbers as exhibits?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. They will retain the same numbers and the ID will be removed to become exhibits. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I only wanted to propose that the Prosecution also distribute -- hands us the diagrams that have been drafted by the Prosecution at the instruction of the witness. So it's -- to share it with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: They weren't given -- the Defence weren't given the diagrams.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: They were. These are the diagrams that were drafted to the instructions of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Because we all have them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not these ones. Maybe I didn't express myself properly. I want to say that the diagrams which were drafted by the witness herself, the sketches, that they be handed to us, the Defence, if, of course, the Prosecution still has them in its possession.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What are they for? I thought Ms. Reidy had explained how these -- the exhibits were actually drawn, upon the instructions of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understood that the witness first drew by hand these diagrams and that then they were -- on the basis of that, they were made on computer. But if that's not the case, then we agree. But if that -- the diagrams were first made by hand by the witness, we're interested in the position of the courtyard, and we'd be -- if such papers do exist, or still exist, we would like to get into possession of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber is of the view that that is a matter between the parties, because --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I understand, quite.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. The Trial Chamber believes that the explanation by the Prosecution is sufficient and that the exhibits, P69, P68, and P70 were properly drawn under the instructions of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps some facts escaped my mind and my recollection, but when you were exchanged, you were taken on a bus over the Sava River to the Croatian side. And as far as I have understood, the front line, so to say, was directly on the other side of the Sava River. And then you told us that when you arrived into Croatia, you saw Mr. Tadic there, so to speak, among enemies. And I would be interested to know who received you there, in which circumstances. Was the Red Cross, for instance present there? And who transported you, as you told us, from that very place which name I don't remember? You said that you went to Grebnice and then further the into Bosnia. Who took care of the transportation from the first place to Grebnice and then further into Bosnia? Could you give us at least a broad view of what really happened there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Honour, but I have to make a few corrections. The name of Grebnice turns up at the end. So from Zasavica, we were brought in along the entire line of Bosanska Gradiska, we had a break there, and the Serbs beat us on the buses. They had the right to do that. And it was the last -- we had contact with Bosna and that is where we crossed the River Sava, the only standing bridge at the time. We crossed over to the town called Dragalici. In Dragalici, the UNPROFOR was waiting for us, as was the International Red Cross, the HVO, the army, the Croatian army in Bosnia, and the HV, the Croatian army, and our guards came. So Mr. Miroslav Vasovic [As interpreted], of the Serbian army, and Serb representatives. This was an exchange one for one, although there were also some corpses here. How the corpses were exchanged, I do not know, but I did see the direction in which they were taken. The exchange involved some 100 civilians, women and children, men, elderly men, a number that crossed to Croatia had to correspond to the numbers of people entering Bosnia. So it was a mutual exchange. In the moment that I became free, the question was raised by the representative of UNPROFOR whether I'm being exchanged on a voluntary basis or whether I would prefer to return to Bosnia. This was the alternative put forward. Now, if I were to return to Bosnia, I was told, I would be free there and I would go to the town, to the town of Samac. So it would be freedom within the Samac camp town. And logically, was -- I could hardly wait to cross over to the other side, where my family and husband was. I said I'd be going to Croatia. We then boarded the buses, organised by HV and HVO, the Croatian army, and the Croatian army in Bosnia. And they took us from Dragalici, via Okucani, Slavonski Brod, to the place, town, called Dubocica, and here we disembarked from the buses, then walked to the ferry, a big ferry, which was transporting vehicles and passengers. It was for the first time the transport organised at such a level of a ferry which was dragged by a rope, a cable. On the other side, in Bosnia, only some 10 kilometres away from Bosanski Samac, the HVO army was waiting for us, which made us board trucks in smaller groups, and they took us to the school which was located in Domaljevac. In this school, people were already there who were waiting for their relatives who were to be exchanged. I had nobody there, because my people were from Croatia, and Croatia there was only a transit. Unfortunately, my husband at the time on that day was on the battlefield. Therefore, from that school in Domaljevac, I was transported to the battlefield where my husband was. As a reception that evening, that night, we had the honour of the gentlemen from Bosanski Samac were shelling us, treating us to such a shelling that it was a question whether anybody would remain alive, any of us would remain alive. This what I am saying, this was my first day of freedom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just ask something of the witness that arose from that, just a clarification for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: You mentioned a name, Mrs. Kapetanovic, which came onto the record as a Miroslav Vasovic, who was I think at the exchange. Could you tell me: Was there somebody called Miroslav Vasovic or is this a mix-up between Miroslav Tadic and Svetozar Vasovic?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible that it was a slip of tongue when I mentioned the name. The man who was in charge of all exchanges and who was present when I was exchanged, so the man who was in charge of all this, was Miroslav Tadic. It is possible that it was a slip of tongue on my part.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Just to clarify: The Miroslav Tadic is the same Miroslav Tadic, the defendant in this case, who you identified when you started your testimony?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely the same man.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Cross-examination? Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Zaric's Defence, I will conduct the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mrs. Kapetanovic. My name is Aleksandar Lazarevic. I am an attorney. And on behalf of the Defence team of Mr. Simo Zaric, I will conduct the cross-examination. Before I alert you to some of the things that have to be borne in mind during cross-examination, let me please, on my behalf and on behalf of my client, express the regret we feel over all of the things that you and your family had to suffer during the war. The questions I'm going to put during the cross-examination are generally formulated in such a way as to allow you to reply with a yes or no. If you do not know an answer to any of the questions put to you, then please tell us so, and if a question is unclear, then again, please tell us so and then I will try to reformulate the question in a clearer manner. I am telling you all this so that we can conduct cross-examination in an efficient manner. Just one more thing I want to alert you to, and this pertains to interpreting, is as follows: You have been answering questions of Ms. Reidy so far. She was addressing you in English, you were replying in B/C/S, so there was no problem there. But since you and I speak the same language, in order to avoid any overlapping and in order to give enough time for interpreters to interpret, then please wait for me to finish my question and then, after making a slight pause, answer the question please. You and I understand each other very well, but the interpreters have to interpret. So that's all I have to say, and if you don't mind, I will start the cross-examination now. Mrs. Kapetanovic, I would like to ask you a few questions that have to do with the time period before April 16th and 17th. I would start with an incident that you mentioned during your examination-in-chief and that had to do with the fact that during the beginning of 1992 you went out frequently with your then boyfriend and now husband and that you frequented the cafe called Valentino. Do you remember telling us about this?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that period very well, and I remember very well that I spoke about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I am interested in an event which took place on February 14th, 1992. Perhaps this date doesn't mean much to you now, but that was the day when a tragedy occurred in the cafe Valentino, in which Bobic Enver and Hadzialijagic Mensur [phoen], two young men, played with a hand grenade and as a result of that were killed. Do you know of this incident that I'm mentioning now?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, I put my question in such a way as to elicit just a yes or no from you, so just please answer in such terms.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Did you -- were you personally present at the time in the cafe Valentino?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on St. Valentine's Day, and I spent that day with my husband in the apartment, so I wasn't present then, but later on I learned what took place there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So after this event, you went to the SUP building, and a large number of people had assembled there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And among other people, there was also an uncle of Hadzialijagic Mensur. His name was Safet Hadzialijagic, and his nickname was Coner; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: There were some indications there implying that the Serbs from the JNA allegedly were to blame for that incident; is that right? Among the people assembled there you heard such insinuations, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: However, Mr. Safet Hadzialijagic at that point came out and calmed down the people in front of the SUP building by telling them that the police was doing its work and that this was apparently a tragic event, accident?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he attempted to calm people.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: But after that, most of the people left the plateau in front of the SUP building and the situation calmed down; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Kapetanovic. That's all I wanted to ask you regarding this event, because you told us that at that time you frequently visited this cafe. Mrs. Kapetanovic, I wanted to ask you something, the reference to which I found in your statement given to the OTP in 2002. I found something, and if you can just please tell me whether this is true or not. When speaking about my client, Mr. Zaric, you said that he was your neighbour and that he was on friendly terms with you and that he used to address you with the nickname Sele, which, if translated, would mean that he addressed you with "sister" or something along those lines. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And as you probably know, his sister's name was also Jelena, so that was probably what prompted him to address you with this term, because you had the same name as his sister.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Madam, during your testimony here, you mentioned the 4th Detachment on many occasions, on numerous occasions. I would like to hear now whether you and I and the rest of us here have the same understanding of what is actually is, what kind of an entity it is. Because of that, I will ask you several questions concerning the 4th Detachment. This is a question where you can't give me a yes or no answer, but please tell me: What do you understand under the term "4th Detachment"?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 4th Detachment was something quite new that appeared in Bosanski Samac. I don't know why it was called the 4th Detachment; however, I know what kind of ideas are behind it, and I knew a lot about the 4th Detachment even before the war broke out.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's take it point by point, then. Tell me, please: Do you know when the 4th Detachment was founded?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date. I wasn't a member of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Kapetanovic, do you know what the 4th Detachment -- what the 1st Detachment is?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We never heard that mentioned in Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What about the 2nd, 3rd, and 5th Detachment? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but I know that the 4th Detachment was in charge of Samac. Later on, I heard about the 6th Detachment and the others you have mentioned, but then, at that time, I only knew about the 4th Detachment and the tasks it had regarding Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you, then, whether you know what the 17th Tactical Group is.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was never interested in such things, and I don't think I am now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Well, I will not insist on it, then. Do you know somebody named Radovan Antic, from Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was my teacher.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether he held some kind of office in the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, do you know what was his function, his office?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He headed the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I will ask you also whether you know Jovo Savic. Do you know that man from Samac?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally never had contact with him, but I do know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Well, we will not go further into that, then. Let me ask you just one more thing. Do you know when the 4th Detachment ceased to exist?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When that happened, I was already at liberty, so I don't know the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Madam, based on the information that we have here, based on numerous testimonies and the documents we have, the 4th Detachment ceased to exist, at the latest, on the 18th of May, 1992, when the army of Republika Srpska was established and when it was transformed into the 5th Battalion, among other formations. Do you know about this fact?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably due to that, there was frequently inconsistencies in my testimony when I spoke about the police and the army. The 4th Detachment had done its job, and that's probably the reason why it ceased to exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, that is probably your opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. This witness had said that she didn't know when the 4th Detachment ceased to exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not going to ask her more about this topic, about how long it lasted and what -- she doesn't have, of course, any military experience, any military knowledge, but anyway, she mentioned the 4th Detachment many times, so I was just challenging what was actually her knowledge about this topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you about some people for whom you have stated that they were members of the 4th Detachment. Cakara, this is the nickname that you used, is that perhaps somebody called Sejdic Naser?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sejdic Naser was an active policeman before the war in Bosanski Samac; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Another name is Caba. You also mentioned this name during your direct examination here. Is that somebody called Ibrahim Trakosevic, in fact?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Was this man an active policeman before the war as well?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Based on their names, I would say that both of them were Muslims. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When you spoke about how you were taken to Crkvina, you mentioned the name of Ranko Popovic. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you know this man Ranko Popovic before the war?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew him very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Was he the most responsible person there in Crkvina? What was your impression?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Savo Cancarevic was the man in charge in Crkvina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, that name is the name of a man I wanted to ask you too. Savo Cancarevic was a policeman before the war as well; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And Simo Krunic, whom we have mentioned today, was also a policeman; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well, then, madam. Now, when I analyse all this that I have asked you about - Cakara, Caba, Cancarvic, Popovic, Simo Krunic - all of these people used to be policemen before the war; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And all of these people, starting on the 16th and on, after the war broke out, continued working in the public security station in Samac, in the Serbian police; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And all of these people, in different ways, were included or involved in arresting you, taking you to Crkvina, bringing you back from Crkvina, taking you to Zasavica, and guarding you in Zasavica; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, this is only a small fragment of people that were involved in these arrests. Mr. Lazarevic, I mentioned these names only because I knew them the best. In my statement, I said that there were some four to five other people whose names I did not mention.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I have to apologise, madam. I do not wish to impute anything to you. All I asked is whether what I told you was true. You confirmed that, and it is a fact that the five of them could not have accomplished that alone, that other people must have been involved. Don't you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mrs. Kapetanovic, you gave evidence here about where your apartment was located. The diagram we received was drawn up pursuant to your instructions by the Prosecution. And now I would like to go back to that diagram for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... assistance of Mr. Usher. I need document P68. It is not ID any more. Yes. We made a decision in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Kapetanovic, please take a good look at this sketch, and after having done so, please put it on the ELMO which is to your right?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... benefit of our clients I would like to have it put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It will be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, we examined this sketch during your examination-in-chief. Was this sketch drawn up in accordance with your instruction? Yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I am now interested in the building itself, the so-called Number 62. Was it drawn in accordance with your instructions?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The position of the building, yes. As to the entrances, I'm not sure right now. Perhaps the doors could be moved to the left or to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, we're not interested in very specific details, just in general. So according to what I can see on this sketch, this building has seven entrances; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says "7" here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Is that what you are claiming, that the building Number 62 has seven entrances?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For some reason I always think that this building had eight entrances, but I was never really interested in that, so I don't know for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So do you allow for the possibility that in addition to these seven, there is an eighth entrance as well?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So there is a possibility, then, that this sketch is not correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, the position and the contours of the building are absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm now talking about the sketch in general. I'm not questioning the position and I'm not questioning whether the building is an L-shaped one. I'm simply talking about the general accuracy of this sketch.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you mean the entrances, I can tell you that yes, it is possible that the entrances were not exactly as drawn here, but I know the building very well, because I lived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... it's 1345.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We'll adjourn and continue tomorrow at 0900 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 2nd day of July 2002, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.45 p.m.,
